card: Fixes intermittent failures in the p2p_tx_download.py functional test by synchronizing mocktime across both nodes and staging time advancements. Previously, unmocked wall-clock time on node 1 allowed transaction request timers to drift, causing node 1 to stall on unresponsive peers and fail during mempool synchronization. This stabilizes test suite execution.
changed_since_previous: Restructured test_inv_block to advance mocktime in explicit stages for both nodes and wait for node 1 to query an inbound peer before triggering timeouts, and removed no-op setmocktime(0) calls.
evidence: PR description: 'Because nodes[1] time was not mocked in test_block_inv, it was possible for wall clock to advance 2s by the time nodes[0] had delivered a tx announcement to it. Then, nodes[1] would request the tx from a test peer, never receive the tx, and fail in sync_mempools().'
Commit 4cc74b2b60 notes that node 0 could announce prematurely, causing node 1 to bypass the blocking inbound peer unless mocktime advancement is explicitly sequenced.
problem: In test_inv_block, node 1 did not have its time mocked while node 0 did. If wall-clock time advanced by two seconds before node 0 announced a transaction, or if peer announcements raced, node 1 would request the transaction from an unresponsive test peer and time out unpredictably, causing sync_mempools() to fail.

risk.why: Touches only functional test code; a mistake would only cause test flakiness or CI failures.

summary: Fixes an intermittent failure in the p2p_tx_download.py functional test by mocking time on node 1 alongside node 0 and staging mocktime increments. It ensures node 1 attempts to download a transaction from an inbound peer first before timing out and retrieving it from node 0.
